question_text: Three pulleys are connected one below another in a chain: the topmost is fixed to a ceiling, and two lighter pulleys hang below it in series, as shown in the figure. Using string-constraint equations, determine how the acceleration of block 2 is related to the acceleration of block 1.
figure_description: A large pulley P₁ is fixed to the ceiling. Below it hang two smaller movable pulleys, P₂ (medium) and P₃ (small), one below the other, and at the bottom sits block 1 (a wide base block); block 2 hangs beside the chain. Three light strings are used. String S₁ passes over P₁: its left end goes straight down to block 1 and its right end goes straight down to the axle of P₂. String S₂ passes over P₂: its left end goes straight down to block 1 and its right end goes straight down to the axle of P₃. String S₃ passes over P₃: its left end goes straight down to block 1 and its right end hangs straight down to block 2. So three string ends are tied to block 1 (one from each pulley) and block 2 hangs from S₃ only. All strings are vertical; pulleys and strings are massless and frictionless. Measure the downward positions of block 1 (x₁), the axle of P₂ (x₃), the axle of P₃ (x₄) and block 2 (x₂) from a fixed horizontal line through P₁; a₁ and a₂ are the accelerations of blocks 1 and 2.

solution.approach: Write the constant-length equation for each of the three strings in turn, then combine the three to connect block 1 and block 2 directly.

steps.text: The string over the top fixed pulley P₁ runs from block 1 to the axle of pulley P₂ (position x₃), so their distances from the reference line add to a constant.
The string S₂ over pulley P₂ (axle at x₃) runs from block 1 to the axle of pulley P₃ (at x₄), both measured relative to P₂'s own position.
The string S₃ over pulley P₃ (axle at x₄) runs from block 1 to block 2, both measured relative to P₃'s own position.
From the first equation, a₃ = −a₁. Put this into the second equation.
Put a₄ = −3a₁ into the third equation and solve for a₂.
steps.why_this_step: Each movable pulley moves with the string above it, and the string over it doubles that motion for the next level while block 1 adds its own; the factors grow 1, 3, 7, so block 2 accelerates seven times as fast as block 1.

final_answer.value: a₂ = −7a₁ (block 2's acceleration is 7 times block 1's acceleration, in the opposite direction)

common_mistakes.text: Writing only the top string's constraint (x₁ + x₃ = constant) and treating everything below P₁ as one body moving with pulley P₂, which gives |a₂| = |a₁|; each movable pulley adds its own constraint.
